headline: Batting collapse: Bangladesh bow out of tri-series after loss to Afghanistan
summary: The Tigers slumped to 160 in 41.2 overs, suffering a fifth successive ODI defeat by Afghanistan and missing the final.
details: Bangladesh's hopes of reaching the tri-series final ended in another batting collapse, as Afghanistan chased down 161 with 7 wickets and 87 balls to spare in Sharjah.
Needing a victory by at least 41 runs to qualify, Bangladesh slumped to 160 in 41.2 overs, suffering a fifth successive ODI defeat by Afghanistan.
Stand-in captain Towhid Hridoy chose to bat first after winning the toss, but the experiment of reshuffling the batting order failed as Bangladesh were reduced to 28 for 4.
Parvez Hossain Emon (70) and Saif Hassan (41) steadied the innings with a 93-run partnership, but the team struggled to accelerate, with four batters making ducks.
Rashid Khan tore through the tail, dismissing Shoriful Islam, Parvez, and two others with successive deliveries to end the innings.
Taskin Ahmed provided a brief glimmer of hope by taking 2 for 36, leaving Afghanistan 39 for 2 early on.
However, Rahmat Shah (67*) and Hashmatullah Shahidi (36*) shared an unbeaten 66-run stand to seal the victory for Afghanistan in 35.3 overs.
Already beaten by Zimbabwe in their opener, Bangladesh now exits the tournament, while Afghanistan advances to face the hosts in Friday's final.
caption:
Another batting collapse. A fifth straight ODI loss to Afghanistan. Bangladesh is out of the tri-series.

Bangladesh's hopes of reaching the tri-series final ended in another batting collapse, as Afghanistan chased down 161 with 7 wickets and 87 balls to spare in Sharjah.

Needing a victory by at least 41 runs to qualify, Bangladesh slumped to 160 in 41.2 overs, suffering a fifth successive ODI defeat by Afghanistan.

Stand-in captain Towhid Hridoy chose to bat first after winning the toss, but the experiment of reshuffling the batting order failed as Bangladesh were reduced to 28 for 4.

Parvez Hossain Emon (70) and Saif Hassan (41) steadied the innings with a 93-run partnership, but the team struggled to accelerate, with four batters making ducks.

Rashid Khan tore through the tail, dismissing Shoriful Islam, Parvez, and two others with successive deliveries to end the innings.

Taskin Ahmed provided a brief glimmer of hope by taking 2 for 36, leaving Afghanistan 39 for 2 early on.

However, Rahmat Shah (67*) and Hashmatullah Shahidi (36*) shared an unbeaten 66-run stand to seal the victory for Afghanistan in 35.3 overs.

Already beaten by Zimbabwe in their opener, Bangladesh now exits the tournament, while Afghanistan advances to face the hosts in Friday's final.

headline: 20+ DJ parties monthly: Additional DIG's house raided for drug use
summary: A senior police officer's Purbachal residence was used for illegal gatherings and drug consumption for nearly a year, despite a police outpost being just 30 yards away.
details: A team from the Detective Branch (DB) raided the Purbachal residence of Abdullah Al Jahir, an additional deputy inspector general (DIG) of police headquarters, uncovering alleged drug use and illegal DJ parties.
DB officials stated that between 20 and 22 DJ parties were organised at the property every month since 2025, with participants recruited through online registration via Airbnb and Travela.
The property was rented out for Tk 18,500 a day for 10 people, with participants paying a registration fee of Tk 600 each. The DIG reportedly received 70 percent of the profits.
Residents and security personnel reported frequent loud music, dancing, and gatherings of affluent university students and bankers, often continuing late into the night or early morning.
The raid occurred despite a six-storey police outpost standing just 30 yards from the property, raising questions about how such activities went unchecked for nearly a year.
During the nearly three-hour raid, detectives recovered several bottles of whisky and vodka, one yaba tablet, equipment for consuming yaba, and a small quantity of 'kush'.
The officer-in-charge of Khilkhet Police Station claimed they were aware of social gatherings but were unaware of the illegal DJ parties and drug consumption.
